title: Reasoning map: grades profile
description: Two separate grades per arrow. strength: if the link is real, how much it moves its target (the size of the coefficient). confidence: how sure we are the link exists as stated (the p-value side). They come apart where it matters most: large if true but unproven is the tail-risk shape. A deductive link's confidence is its premises' confidence, never more. A definition or identity gets a confidence and no strength, because it moves nothing on its own.

confidence.description: established: replicated, survives controls. well-supported: good identification, limited era or sample. suggestive: directionally indicated, effect size unstable. contested: serious people disagree; name both sides. folklore: circulates widely, no defensible source.
